headings.text: # tsk-7l9-2 D8: fgos-gateway's first async dependency -- the gateway's REST
# surface (D1/D7) is what needs one; the TUI/orchestrator code stays fully
# synchronous and untouched.
# tsk-7l9-3: bumped 0.7 -> 0.8 -- required by `rmcp`'s streamable-http-server
# transport (mcp.rs), which only supports axum ^0.8. Breaking route-syntax
# change (`:id` -> `{id}`) rewritten across every existing route in
# gateway.rs's `build_router`; no other breaking change touches this crate
# (State/middleware::from_fn_with_state/Json extraction are unaffected).
# tsk-7l9-3 D1: MCP surface's server SDK -- the official
# modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk, tokio-async, mounts its
# `transport::streamable_http_server::StreamableHttpService` directly onto an
# existing `axum::Router` via `.nest_service()` (confirmed against the SDK's
# own `examples/servers/src/counter_streamhttp.rs`), so `search`/`execute`
# ride the SAME router/port `tsk-7l9-2`'s REST surface already serves -- no
# second process, no second listener. `mcpkit-axum` (this plan's original
# pick alongside rmcp) turned out to be a wholly separate, non-composable MCP
# SDK (`mcpkit-core`/`mcpkit-server`/`mcpkit-transport`, unrelated to rmcp) --
# dropped, rmcp alone covers the whole surface.
# tsk-7l9-3 D1: `execute`'s bound-function scripting language (Approach's own
# rhai-over-mlua pick: pure Rust, no vendored-C/system-Lua dependency, matches
# D1's "no extra runtime layer" rationale). `serde` feature turns bound
# function results (serde_json::Value) into Rhai `Dynamic` values and back.
# tsk-7l9-3: `search`'s only new data need -- parses the OpenAPI contract
# (`docs/contracts/fgos-gateway-api-v1.yaml`) into a queryable operation list
# instead of serving it as an opaque string the way `/contract` already does.
# tsk-54y: CORS layer for `build_router` -- the web client (a separate
# static bundle, D2 of docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard-plan-realignment/
# CONTEXT.md) is not guaranteed to share origin with the gateway. Version
# resolved by `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's existing axum 0.8
# dependency graph (docs/history/tsk-54y-gateway-cors-bind/plan.md).
# tsk-48w (D14 of docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard-plan-realignment/
# CONTEXT.md): embeds apps/fgos-gateway/web's built bundle into the binary so
# the "máy được chọn" can serve it with no separate deploy step.
# Versions resolved by real `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's
# existing dependency graph (docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/plan.md,
# "NẮN LẠI P1 tsk-48w"): rust-embed 8.12.0, axum-embed 0.1.0, same
# rust-embed major line the reference implementation herdr-gateway pins.
# tsk-6arn (D8): Cloudflare Access as auth layer 2, additive to the
# Bearer token layer already shipped (tsk-7l9). Ported from the reference
# implementation herdr-gateway (crate herdr-go, src/web/cf_access.rs).
# Versions resolved by real `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's
# existing dependency graph -- differ from the reference's own pins
# (jsonwebtoken 9->11, reqwest 0.12->0.13; reqwest's TLS feature was
# renamed `rustls-tls`->`rustls` between those versions, confirmed by a
# real dry-run failure before the correction). `jsonwebtoken`'s
# `aws_lc_rs` feature is required explicitly -- v11 ships neither crypto
# backend by default (real runtime panic caught at Execute: "Could not
# automatically determine the process-level CryptoProvider... make sure
# exactly one of the 'rust_crypto' and 'aws_lc_rs' features is enabled"),
# and `aws_lc_rs` matches the backend `reqwest`'s own `rustls` feature
# already pulls in, avoiding a second, competing provider in the same
# binary.
